findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the shard fan-out source: either define the 'by repository surface' shard map explicitly in this plan/session log, or cite the specific document that actually contains a surface-based fan-out, since docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md defines only a code-health perspective fan-out.
evidence: docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md line 3: 'A repeatable recipe for the periodic "principal-engineer maintenance audit" of rebar: detect code debt, smells, architectural decay ... doc drift'
docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md lines 9-12: 'fan out one subagent per *perspective* (size, duplication, architecture, complexity, docs, dead-code, tests)'
docs/README.md line 163-164: describes it as 'the repeatable recipe for the periodic principal-engineer code-health audit'

The plan is a prose/comment/documentation-taxonomy audit sharded 'by repository surface' (Scope enumerates root docs, docs/, external docs, comments), which the runbook's perspective-based method does not define.
findings.finding: The plan states the shard fan-out 'by repository surface follows docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md', but that runbook actually defines a fan-out by code-health PERSPECTIVE (size, duplication, architecture, complexity, docs, dead-code, tests) for a periodic code-health/complexity audit, not a documentation/prose/comment audit sharded by repository surface. The named file exists but does not supply the surface-based sharding scheme the plan attributes to it.
findings.location: Approach section: 'The fan-out by repository surface follows docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md.'
scenarios: Exploration agents open the runbook to derive their non-overlapping shard boundaries and find perspective lanes (complexity, dead-code) rather than the documentation-surface shards the plan's Scope lists.
The 'Exploration agents inspect non-overlapping shards' acceptance criterion cannot be verified against a shard map the referenced file does not contain.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the repository-surface shard map inside this plan (or a runbook section that actually enumerates documentation surfaces), rather than relying on maintenance-audit-runbook.md, which shards by code-health perspective and provides no surface partition.
evidence: Plan: 'The fan-out by repository surface follows docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md. Separate shards reduce omissions within large document families.'

docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md line 9-13: 'fan out one subagent per *perspective* (size, duplication, architecture, complexity, docs, dead-code, tests)' — sharding is by perspective, not by documentation surface
The runbook's scans target src/*.py (LOC, radon cc, vulture, jscpd) and code-health, not the documentation surfaces (root docs, docs/, external guides, help, MCP descriptions) this audit scopes
findings.finding: The plan grounds its shard fan-out in docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md, but that runbook shards by analysis PERSPECTIVE (size, duplication, architecture, complexity, docs, dead-code, tests) for a code-health audit and contains no repository-surface shard map. The cited procedure does not supply the 'fan-out by repository surface' the plan depends on, leaving the non-overlapping-shard mechanism (AC-6) under-specified.
findings.location: Approach section: 'The fan-out by repository surface follows docs/maintenance-audit-runbook.md.'
scenarios: Exploration agents receive no concrete surface-to-shard map, so shards overlap or leave scoped surfaces uncovered, undermining AC-1 (inventory names every surface) and AC-6 (non-overlapping shards).
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the surface shards directly in the Approach (aligned with the four Scope bullets: root/metadata/policy, docs/ internal+ADRs, external/help/MCP/examples, source+test+config comments) and state the disjoint-partition rule, so AC-6 has a concrete, verifiable basis independent of the code-health runbook.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define how concurrent shard reports are written to the shared session log (per-shard section ownership or separate files merged at consolidation) so reports cannot interleave or overwrite.
evidence: 'Ask independent agents to inspect non-overlapping shards.'
AC: 'Verification uses one session log report for each shard.' -- multiple agents produce reports into one log without stated write ownership.
findings.finding: The session log is shared write state: exploration agents write one report per shard and filtering agents consume the consolidated proposals, but the plan does not define ownership or concurrency discipline for concurrent shard-report writes into the shared log.
findings.location: Approach: 'Record findings in a session log. Ask independent agents to inspect non-overlapping shards.'
findings.suggested_fix: State that each exploration agent writes its shard report to a distinct, agent-owned section or file, and that consolidation merges them into the coverage table, so no two agents write the same region concurrently.
